thread:
Taylor M: Morning — noticed an uptick in SLA misses for first-owner contact overnight, looks like a cluster of micro-reassigns plus enrichment timeouts. p95 lead-handshake latency jumped and customer-facing SLA alerts tripped.
Rina H: Yep. Found a pattern: enrichment p95 > 25s coincides with higher RR churn. We should avoid naive reassigns during noisy enrichment windows.
Oliver P: Instead of pure hold-or-fast paths, what if we introduce a sampling-based backstop policy: when enrichment p95 > threshold, we sample X% of leads into a backstop queue that gets special handling (sticky owner + rehydrate job) while others follow fast path?
Sam K: Interesting. Sampling keeps load down but protects enough signals to measure impact. What thresholds and sample size?
Taylor M: Proposal: when region_enrichment_p95 > 25s, enable backstop sampling at 10%. For sampled leads: mark backstop=true, owner gets sticky_ttl += 1h, and assignment service will skip reassigns for backstop_duration = 7m. For non-sampled leads run normal hybrid assign.
Rina H: Implementation sketch for HubSpot workflow (pseudo):
```
# HubSpot: set backstop marker based on feature gate + sampling
IF feature_flag('handoff_backstop') == true AND region_p95_enrich > 25s THEN
  IF random() < 0.10 THEN set lead.property 'backstop' = 'true' AND set 'backstop_until' = now + 7m
  ELSE set 'backstop' = 'false'
END
```
Oliver P: On the CRM write side add a backstop guard: don't overwrite owner if lead.backstop == true OR now < backstop_until. Also add idempotency_key = assignment.request_id to avoid duplicate writes from webhook retries.
Sam K: Round-robin tuning: add per-lead cooldown (rr_cooldown=120s) and max_attempts=3 before escalating to backstop queue. Add jitter: cooldown += rand(0,30s). This should prevent cascades when retries line up.
Taylor M: Observability hooks: add metrics handoff.backstop_rate, handoff.sla_violation_pct, handoff.rr_cooldown_median, handoff.owner_churn_rate. Dashboards should show region breakdown.
Rina H: Playbook for ops/SDR:
1) If handoff.backstop_rate > 15% or sla_violation_pct rises -> pause backstop sampling and run rehydrate pipeline.
2) If sample leads show improved stability -> increase sample to 25% and then consider wider guard.
3) For persistent noise, disable RR entirely for the region and route to manual triage.
Oliver P: Rollout plan: feature flag 'handoff_backstop' default=false. Canary to one EMEA region night window for 48h. Success criteria: owner_churn_rate down >= 40% AND sla_violation_pct down >= 30% without pushing response-time >10% for non-sampled leads.
Sam K: PR description stub: "handoff backstop sampling: feature-flagged sampling guard that protects a subset of leads during enrichment noise; adds rr cooldown, idempotent CRM writes, metrics, and ops playbook. Canary EMEA nights."
Taylor M: Also add a small experiment to A/B test: sampled leads get sticky + backstop, control leads get sticky only when claim_count > 2. Collect NPS-ish proxy: first-contact within 15m.
Rina H: One more safety: if deferred queue length > 500, auto-rate-limit new deferred entries and send alert to #sales-inbound. ops-bot can auto-run rehydrate job.
ops-bot: [automated] Feature flag created: handoff_backstop (default=false). Monitors: marketing.handoff.backstop_rate, marketing.handoff.sla_violation_pct.
Oliver P: Can we add a tiny UI toggle in Console to show backstop sample hits and requeue leads? Ops would love that.
Sam K: I'll add metric panels and an alert runbook to the PR. Also drafting tests for idempotency + rr cooldown jitter.
Taylor M: Great. 10m sync in 20 to assign owners for PR and dashboard cards. Goal: reduce noisy reassigns and protect SLA without large customer impact. Post updates here after the sync. :white_check_mark:
